verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves of the arithmetic are company wire-release figures, not obscure data. $852.4M RPO at 2026-01-31 was in the 2026-03-19 FY26 release (and repeated verbatim in trade coverage), and $816M at 2026-04-30 was in the 2026-06-04 Q1 FY27 release and spoken aloud on the call. The subtraction is trivial and available to anyone who read both press releases; what is genuinely unreported is the framing 'RPO book-to-bill 0.6'. But the forward limb of the claim - that the May-July quarter contains 'no announced nine-figure booking at all, only two seven-figure deals' - is factually wrong as an enumeration: Planet press-released an 8-figure, $22M NGA Luno B option-year extension plus a new NGA/DIU Global Monitoring Service award on 2026-06-04, inside the 1 May - 31 July window, and it was picked up by Defense Daily and Via Satellite the same day. The hunter also selects the one book metric that fell and ignores the one management actually guides on: backlog rose $900M -> $906M over the same quarter, i.e. total bookings roughly matched revenue rather than collapsing to 0.6x. RPO for this name is lumpy by construction (it was +106% YoY at FY26 end on the German/NATO-type multi-year awards), so one $36M sequential draw is not evidence of demand deceleration and the magnitude is genuinely contested. Discounted heavily for the published inputs and the broken forward premise; credited for the fact that no preview or sell-side note frames this quarter as a bookings problem.

prior_publication.what_it_says: FY26 close: RPO approximately $852.4M, up ~106% YoY; end-of-period backlog over $900M.
Q1 FY27: revenue $94.2M, RPO approximately $816M (up 81% YoY), backlog approximately $906M (up 72% YoY).

NGA exercised a one-year, $22M Luno B option for maritime domain awareness - an 8-figure award announced inside the May-July quarter, contradicting the claim that only two 7-figure deals were announced.
Q2 preview frames backlog at ~$906M, +72% YoY, as 'strong future revenue visibility' - the consensus narrative is backlog strength, not sequential RPO erosion.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: I am using the reaction history and the run-in, not the drawdown. The -25.98% reaction on 2026-06-04 is the date the $816M figure became public, so if the market cared about sequential RPO it had its chance and the contemporaneous wire copy attributes that move to the $1.5B ATM equity offering, the 52-54% full-year gross-margin guide-down from 56% and $80-95M capex, not to bookings. The -16.1% 20-day run-in is dated to the post-SpaceX-IPO space-sector de-rating and the ATM overhang, per Benzinga 2026-08-24, so it is not claim-specific evidence for this one. There is no 25-delta skew for this name and put/call OI is 0.59 (call-heavy), so I make no appeal to the options market on direction. If this specific claim were in the price I would expect at least one preview to name RPO or bookings as the swing item; none of the three previews I read does.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Q2 FY27 RPO print materially below $816M with backlog also down, or evidence that a sell-side note between June and September had already modelled a second sequential RPO decline, would move this in opposite directions.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The load-bearing fact is a line in Planet's own Q3 FY26 wire release on 2025-12-10 - the URL path segment 20251210 confirms the year, so this is a prior-fiscal-year document, not a fresh one - and it was reproduced by Intelligence Community News and the trade press at the time. 'Anchor US intelligence contract with an expiry inside the next few quarters' is therefore in the wire copy, and EOCL budget risk for the commercial EO operators is one of the most worn narratives in the sector after BlackSky's publicly reported EOCL revenue gap. Two things then cut the residual hard. First, the absence of a renewal press release is close to worthless as evidence: Planet has never press-released a baseline EOCL renewal as a standalone item - the December 2025 renewal itself was disclosed only inside the quarterly release - so 'no PR since June' is exactly what the base rate predicts whether or not the contract renewed. Second, and more damaging, management raised FY27 revenue guidance from $415-440M to $425-441M on 2026-06-04, four weeks before the stated expiry and with full knowledge of it. Either they had renewal visibility or they had already absorbed the loss into the guide; on both branches the guidance the market is marking against already reflects it. Size is real but modest: ~$13.2M for the period, ~$21M annualised, roughly 5% of the FY27 revenue midpoint, against a segment growing 65% YoY. The unpublished residual is the specific observation that the expiry fell inside the quarter now being reported.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q3 FY26 release states the NRO renewed the baseline EOCL contract for PlanetScope broad-area monitoring for $13.2M through June 2026, plus a CLIN framework for high-resolution Pelican orders.

Planet Federal's EOCL award runs an initial period of up to five years with options extending to a ten-year total performance term - the annual baseline task-order renewal is the routine mechanism, not a cliff.
FY27 revenue guidance raised to $425-441M and Q2 guided to $102-107M, issued four weeks before the stated June 2026 EOCL baseline expiry.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 2025-12-10 print, which is the document carrying this disclosure, moved +35.01% - the market read that release as good news, so the '$13.2M through June 2026' line was absorbed as a renewal, not as an expiry warning. That is the pricing event and it went the other way. I am not using the -62.9% drawdown from the 52-week high as evidence here: the contemporaneous reporting attributes it to the $1.5B ATM and the space-sector selloff, and if the market were specifically pricing a lost NRO baseline I would expect it in preview copy - the 2026-09-02 Investing.com preview mentions NGA extensions and defence momentum and does not raise the NRO baseline at all. No 25-delta skew exists for this name, so I make no options argument.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the Q2 FY27 release is silent on the NRO baseline while disclosing every other renewal, or if a US-government data-subscription revenue line comes in flat-to-down sequentially, the residual here is much larger than 50 implies.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is published guidance, twice over, and it is the single most-reported thing about this stock in 2026. FY27 adjusted EBITDA of breakeven-to-$10M against FY26 actual $15.5M was issued 2026-03-19 and reaffirmed alongside the revenue and gross-margin raises on 2026-06-04, and it is the stated cause of the -25.98% reaction that day: the wire copy explicitly said the $5M midpoint sat below the $8.23M consensus. Chartmill headlined it 'Revenue Beat Fails to Lift Stock as Guidance Disappoints'; Benzinga and Motley Fool both ran follow-ups on the margin guide-down from 56% to 52-54% plus $80-95M capex. The 2026-09-02 previews are still carrying it forward - 'investors will watch whether growth investments pressure near-term earnings.' The 'arithmetically requires ~30% opex growth' step is inference from published numbers, not new information, and Q1 opex of $85.3M is in the same release. The only genuinely unpublished datum is the 114 open requisitions on the job board, which is a soft proxy with no dollar figure attached and which management has already pre-announced in words ('continue to invest in our global sales and marketing organization'). Under the stated anchors, restating published guidance sits at 90-100; I hold at 90 only for the job-board sliver.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Revenue beat but FY27 EBITDA guidance of $5M at the midpoint came in below the $8.23M analyst estimate, and the stock fell.
FY27 revenue $425-441M, non-GAAP gross margin 52-54%, adjusted EBITDA breakeven to $10M; Q1 opex $85.3M split R&D $33.4M / S&M $22.8M / G&A $29.1M.

Attributes the decline to margin compression, the guided step down from 56% to 52-54%, high capex of $80-95M and the $1.5B ATM equity offering, with options pricing high vol into the 3 September print.
Preview flags that the 56% gross margin 'provides room to scale, but investors will watch whether growth investments pressure near-term earnings.'

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 2026-06-04 reaction of -25.98% is the price move on this exact information, on the exact date it became known, and the contemporaneous wire copy names the EBITDA/margin/capex guide as a primary cause alongside the ATM. That is the cleanest 'already in the price' evidence in this brief. The continued slide to $19.06 (-62.9% from the 52-week high) is consistent with the market having fully de-rated the profitability path. I make no skew argument - there is none for this name and put/call OI at 0.59 is call-heavy, which if anything argues against reading the tape as an unpriced bear case.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Only an actual cut to the FY27 EBITDA range below zero, or Q2 opex materially above the ~30% growth path the guide implies, would make this new rather than a restatement.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Attacking the bullish one as hard as the bears: this is the weakest of the four on novelty. Every fact in it was issued by Planet itself on Business Wire and syndicated - the three-Pelican launch on 2026-05-03 (URL segment 20260503 confirms the year), first light including Sweden's first sovereign satellite on 2026-05-14, the Pelican-11 shipment on 2026-06-02, and the Pelican-11 Gen-2 tech-demo launch on Transporter-17 on 2026-07-06/07, with Reuters and TradingView carrying the shipment and launch. Management then guided Q2 FY27 revenue to $102-107M on 2026-06-04, after the May launch had already happened and with Pelican-11 already at Vandenberg, and consensus has settled at $104.1M - dead on the guide midpoint - with analysts reconfirming estimates over the last 30 days. So 'launches did not slip, therefore the $102-107M guide holds' is not a discovery; it is the consensus, restated. The mechanism is also thinner than presented: the large majority of Planet's revenue is recurring data subscription that does not depend on a launch clearing inside the window, and the one line that genuinely does - dedicated satellite services milestone recognition, e.g. the Swedish sovereign satellite - had its launch and first light press-released twelve and one weeks before management set the guide. The residual is only that a market this beaten up may have stopped assuming execution, and there is a sliver of Gen-2 30cm-timeline optionality that is not in any number.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Planet announces the launch of three additional high-resolution Pelican satellites.
First light from the May launch, including imagery from Sweden's first sovereign satellite - the delivery milestone behind satellite-services recognition.
Pelican-11, the Gen-2 technology demonstrator, launched on SpaceX Transporter-17 from Vandenberg; initial contact made and commissioning begun.
Consensus Q2 revenue $104.12M (+43.3% YoY), at the midpoint of the company's $102-107M guide, with analysts reconfirming estimates over the last 30 days.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No move in the baseline is attributable to either launch: the stock fell through May, June and July anyway (-16.1% over the last 20 days alone) while both launches were succeeding, which is the strongest possible demonstration that on-schedule launches were already assumed and carry no premium. Consensus sitting exactly on the guide midpoint is the direct statement that 'the guide holds' is the priced case. I note the reaction history's median absolute move of 25.98% is well above the 18.23% option-implied move, so this name is capable of a large upside gap - but that is a statement about variance, not about this claim being unpriced.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that consensus had cut Q2 revenue below the guide low on launch-slippage fears, or disclosure that a large satellite-services milestone recognises in Q2 that sell-side had modelled in Q3, would make this genuinely new.

interactions: Substantial source overlap that the scorer should collapse. PL#0 and PL#2 are both differenced out of the same two company earnings releases - the FY26 Q4 release of 2026-03-19 (RPO $852.4M, backlog >$900M, FY26 adj EBITDA $15.5M, first FY27 guide $415-440M / 50-52% GM / $0-10M EBITDA) and the Q1 FY27 release of 2026-06-04 (RPO $816M, backlog $906M, revenue $94.2M, opex $85.3M, raised guide $425-441M / 52-54% / $0-10M EBITDA, Q2 guide $102-107M). They are one source cluster and should count once, at the larger residual, which is PL#0. PL#1 rests on a third, older document from a prior fiscal year - the Q3 FY26 release of 2025-12-10 - so it is a separate cluster, but note that its implication is neutralised by the 2026-06-04 release that PL#0 and PL#2 both use, because that is where management raised guidance with the June 2026 EOCL expiry already known. PL#0 and PL#3 are near mirrors on the same quarter and partly cancel: PL#0 argues the May-July quarter was commercially barren while PL#3 argues it executed cleanly, and the public record supports PL#3's side of that - the quarter contained a press-released $22M NGA Luno B option year and a new NGA/DIU award on 2026-06-04, two successful launches, the Scottish Government deal on 2026-07-30, and it closed with backlog up. PL#0's enumeration of the quarter's announced bookings as 'only two seven-figure deals' is contradicted by that $22M award and is the specific limb on which I priced PL#0 up. Finally, PL#2's job-board datum (114 open requisitions, heavily EMEA quota-bearing sales) is the only item in the brief with no published source behind it, and it argues in the same direction as PL#0's demand-deceleration thesis while being evidence of the opposite - aggressive commercial hiring.
